page.title: Marbella Boat Charter Weather in December: What to Expect

data.meta_description: Planning a marbella boat charter weather december? Expect 15-18°C, calm seas, and blue skies. Book your winter cruise today.
data.summary: December in Marbella offers mild weather for boat charters, with average highs of 18°C and calm Mediterranean seas. This guide covers temperatures, wind conditions, and what to expect for a comfortable winter cruise.
key_facts: Sunshine: 6 hours per day on average

faq.q: Can you charter a boat in Marbella in December?
faq.a: Yes, boat charters run year-round from Puerto Banús. December is a quieter, more relaxed time with fewer crowds. All our boats, including the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39, are available. The weather is mild enough for a comfortable cruise, especially between 11am and 4pm.

faq.q: What is the average temperature in Marbella in December?
faq.a: Daytime highs average 18°C, dropping to around 10°C in the evening. Sea temperatures sit at 16-17°C. While swimming is possible for the hardy, most guests prefer to enjoy the views and onboard amenities rather than take a dip.

faq.q: How windy is it in Marbella in December?
faq.a: Wind speeds typically range from 10 to 15 knots, with calm seas in sheltered areas like the coast from Puerto Banús to Cabopino. Occasional stronger Levante winds can occur, but your skipper will adjust the route to ensure a smooth ride.

faq.q: Is December a good time for a boat party in Marbella?
faq.a: Yes, December is excellent for a private celebration or corporate event. The mild weather means you can enjoy the flybridge or sundeck without overheating. The Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a popular choice for festive charters, with free jet ski included.

faq.q: What should I wear for a December boat charter in Marbella?
faq.a: Layers are key. Start with a long-sleeve top or light jumper, bring a windproof jacket or fleece, and wear comfortable trousers. Sunglasses and sunscreen are still advisable—the sun can be strong even in winter. Non-slip shoes are recommended.

faq.q: Do you offer shorter charters in December?
faq.a: Yes, we offer 2-hour and 4-hour charters, though 4+ hours are more popular to make the most of daylight. The Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) cost €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours, including skipper, drinks, and VAT.

faq.q: What are the best destinations for a December boat trip?
faq.a: Popular winter routes include cruising the Marbella coastline to Cabopino, or heading west toward Estepona. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are sheltered coves ideal for a peaceful stop. The views of La Concha mountain are particularly clear in winter.

faq.q: Is the sea rough in Marbella in December?
faq.a: Generally no. The Mediterranean is calm in December, with average wave heights under 1 metre. Your skipper will monitor conditions and choose the safest route. If you're prone to seasickness, the larger boats like the Ferretti 94 (29m) offer a more stable ride.

data.body_html:
Planning a marbella boat charter weather december? You might be surprised how pleasant a winter cruise can be. With average highs of 18°C, six hours of daily sunshine, and calm Mediterranean seas, December offers a unique opportunity to enjoy the Costa del Sol without the summer crowds. All our boats depart year-round from Puerto Banús, and this guide covers exactly what to expect—temperatures, wind, sea conditions, and how to dress for a comfortable day on the water.

December Temperatures in Marbella

Daytime temperatures in Marbella during December typically range from 15°C to 18°C. Early mornings and late afternoons can dip to around 10°C, so the sweet spot for chartering is between 11am and 4pm. The sea temperature hovers at 16-17°C—swimmable for the brave, but most guests prefer to stay dry and enjoy the heated cabin or wrap up on deck. The sun feels warm when it's out, especially in sheltered spots, and the light is perfect for photography, with La Concha mountain often crystal clear in the background.

Wind and Sea Conditions

December is generally a calm month for the Mediterranean along the Marbella coast. Prevailing winds are light, usually 10-15 knots, and seas are flat to slight. The occasional Levante wind can pick up, but your licensed skipper will adjust the route to keep the ride comfortable. The coastline from Puerto Banús to Cabopino and Estepona is well-sheltered. For larger groups, the Boat Rental Marbella fleet includes stable vessels like the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) and the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax), which handle any chop with ease.

Sunshine and Daylight Hours

December offers around 6 hours of direct sunshine per day, with sunrise at approximately 8:20am and sunset by 6:10pm. This gives you a solid window for a half-day or full-day charter. Cloud cover is variable, but many December days are partly cloudy with long sunny spells. Rain is infrequent—only 4-6 rainy days on average—so the odds are in your favour. A 4-hour charter (e.g., 11am-3pm) is a popular choice, allowing you to enjoy the best light and warmth.

What to Wear and Bring

Layering is the golden rule for a December boat charter. Start with a long-sleeve top or light jumper, add a windproof jacket or fleece, and wear comfortable trousers or jeans. Non-slip shoes are recommended. Don't forget sunglasses and sunscreen—the UV index can still be moderate, and glare off the water is strong. A light scarf or hat can help against the sea breeze. All our charters include water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks, so you only need to bring your personal items.

Best Boats for a Winter Charter

For smaller groups (up to 9 pax), the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, €749/2h) is a cosy choice with a heated interior. For up to 11 pax, the Azimut 39 (12.5m, same price) offers a similar experience. Larger parties will appreciate the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax, from €4,719/4h including a free jet ski) or the Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax, pricing on request). All boats depart from Puerto Banús and include a licensed skipper, fuel, insurance, and 21% Spanish VAT. For specific rates on other vessels, contact us via WhatsApp.

Popular December Routes

Winter routes focus on sheltered coastal cruising. A classic option is heading east from Puerto Banús toward Cabopino, passing the Golden Mile and Marbella Marina. Alternatively, go west to Estepona or Sotogrande, with stops at Cala del Faro or Cala Cortés for a quiet anchorage. The views of the Sierra Blanca and La Concha are often clearer in winter than in summer due to lower humidity. Your skipper will tailor the itinerary to the day's conditions.

Booking Tips for December

December is a low season, so availability is generally good, but weekends and Christmas week can book up. We recommend reserving at least a few days in advance. The Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) are the most affordable at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. For a festive touch, consider the Mangusta 80 (Grey) or K80—both 24m and 12 pax. All prices include skipper, drinks, snacks, and VAT. For any other boat, contact us via WhatsApp for a personalised quote.
